primitives.name: Collider Orientation Rule
primitives.verbatim_quote: <<<PAGE 4>>> R0′d: For all unshielded triples A∗-◦B◦-∗C and for all unshielded triples A∗→B◦-∗C: If B /∈SAC, then mark the unshielded triple for orientation as collider A∗→B←∗C.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A, B, C': 'variables in a causal graph', 'SAC': 'set of variables that are ancestors of C and descendants of A'}
primitives.assumptions: Unshielded triple exists; B is not in the set of ancestors of C and descendants of A.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When B is in SAC, the triple cannot be oriented as a collider.

layer2.mapping: The rule maps conditional independence constraints to causal graph orientations via ancestral relationships.
layer2.telemetry: Verification of collider orientation through ancestral exclusion.

primitives.name: Parent-to-Child Orientation Rule
primitives.verbatim_quote: R1′: For all unshielded triples A∗→ ∗B◦-⋆ ∗C: If SAC is weakly minimal and B ∈SAC, then mark the edge between B and C for orientation as B→ ∗C.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A, B, C': 'variables in a causal graph', 'SAC': 'set of variables that are ancestors of C and descendants of A', 'weakly minimal': 'minimal set satisfying conditional independence constraints'}
primitives.assumptions: SAC is weakly minimal; B is in SAC.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If SAC is not weakly minimal or B is not in SAC, no orientation is applied.

layer2.mapping: Derives directed edge from conditional independence structure using weak minimality.
layer2.telemetry: Edge orientation based on weak minimality of ancestral sets.

primitives.name: Path Extension Rule
primitives.verbatim_quote: R2′: For all A→ ∗B∗→ ∗C with A⋆-◦ ∗C and for all A∗→ ∗B→ ∗C with A⋆-◦ ∗C: Mark the edge between A and C for orientation as A⋆→ ∗C.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A, B, C': 'variables in a causal graph', 'A⋆-◦ ∗C': 'unshielded edge between A and C'}
primitives.assumptions: A and C are unshielded; B is part of a directed path from A to C.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When A and C are not unshielded, or B does not lie on a directed path, no orientation occurs.

layer2.mapping: Extends directed paths in causal graphs by transitivity under unshielded conditions.
layer2.telemetry: Path extension verified by checking unshielded edge and intermediate node connectivity.

R0′d identifies colliders by excluding intermediate nodes from ancestral sets, ensuring no spurious associations. R1′ leverages weak minimality to direct edges from parents to children, refining causal directionality. R2′ extends paths when unshielded edges exist, enabling more complex causal inferences. Each rule operates under specific conditional independence constraints, forming a coherent system for causal discovery. Failure modes include violations of weak minimality or incorrect identification of ancestral relationships, leading to misoriented edges. The interplay of these rules ensures robustness against noise while maintaining theoretical soundness.
